18.55ab: He should give the exposition according to the chapter; he shall not meet an untimely death.
18.55cd: Even if dead, he is gradually cooked in the multitude of hells.
18.56ab: Knowing this, O Great Goddess, one should acquire what is for one's own welfare.
18.56cd: Even a disciple who receives [instruction] through improper means falls into hell.
18.57ab: Yet he does not obtain it at that time; my word is indeed infallible.

18.57cd: Having attained knowledge through the proper method, if he subsequently does not proceed [to realization], 18.58ab: then the wise one should perform the removal of his consciousness (vijñānāpahṛti). 18.58cd:
The knower of yoga, having meditated upon him and established him before him in his very own form, [should act].
18.59ab: One should arrange the sixfold path within his body as previously described.
18.59cd: Then, having observed that lamp at the tip of his thumb, he should lead it forth in sequence. 18.60ab: With one-pointed mind, he should withdraw the radiance and lead it to the dvādaśānta.

18.60cd: Then, having contemplated him there as having attained oneness with Śiva, 18.61ab: one should meditate there upon that which is of the nature of darkness (tamas), characterized by the tendency toward concealment;
18.61cd: [one should meditate on] her falling along that path until she reaches the tip of the big toe.
18.62ab: One should meditate on [him] as having the luster of thick collyrium, both externally and internally. 18.62cd: By this method, for that dull-witted and evil-minded one, 18.63ab:
Knowledge, mantras, sciences, and the like do not provide any assistance.
18.63cd: For by the mere intention of the mind, [the result] arises even for one who has not [physically] seen [the object].
18.64ab: This applies in some way to one who has perceived an ever-harming [being].
18.64cd: Or else, having meditated on the sun's orb as being in front, it should be severed.
18.65ab: One should contemplate him as being seized by the power of Svarbhānu;
18.65cd: possessed of great anger on account of thousands of offenses.
18.66ab: One should perform this rite for the sake of sport, and never for any other purpose.

18.66cd: One who has fallen away from this method and from another [method] of higher knowledge, 18.67ab: cannot be joined [to the path] again as long as he has not been raised up by that very same [method].
18.67cd: But one whose mind is drawn by compassion, having performed his purification, [may succeed].
18.68ab: Through intense expiations such as breath-control (prāṇāyāma) prescribed by the rules of scripture, 18.68cd:
one should then perform his initiation according to the path previously described. 18.69ab:
Thereafter, with a mind focused on nothing else, he obtains the entire fruit from that.
18.69cd: Having understood this, the wise person should strive diligently to approach a guru. 18.70ab: For from him arises contentment, which consists of the nectar of the knowledge of Śiva.
18.70cd: One should not investigate his conduct, whether it be auspicious or inauspicious.
18.71ab: He alone discerns whether that [action] is appropriate or indeed inappropriate;
18.71cd: when he is attached to improper acts that take away both lives, 18.72ab: then he must be restrained by a wise man who bows before him.
18.72cd: Even if he is being strongly dissuaded by him, if he does not turn back, 18.73ab: then, having gone elsewhere to some other place, he should contemplate only Śiva.
18.73cd: This method of yoga has been declared in brief for the benefit of yogins.
18.74ab: Here there is neither purity nor impurity, nor any deliberation regarding what is fit to be eaten and so forth;
18.74cd: neither duality nor non-duality, nor the worship of external signs and the like; 18.75ab: nor even the renunciation of those things, nor indeed the state of possessing nothing at all.
18.75cd: Or even the state of possessing belongings, such as the gathering of matted hair, ashes, and so forth;

18.76ab: the renunciation of those things, as well as the performance or non-performance of vows and other observances; 18.76cd: the entering of sacred sites and the like, and the observance of pledges and other rules.
18.77ab: Neither another’s form, marks, and so forth, nor name, lineage, and the like, 18.77cd: is prescribed for this [state], nor is anything prohibited.
18.78ab: Whatever is prescribed here, or likewise whatever is prohibited, [all that pertains to the previous state].
18.78cd: But here, O Goddess of gods, this is prescribed as a rule:
18.79ab: The yogin must, with great effort, stabilize the mind upon reality (tattva). 18.79cd: And in whatever way that [stabilization] may occur for him, in that very way he should practice.
But one whose mind is unwavering in reality, even while enjoying sense objects,
is not touched by defects, just as a lotus leaf is not touched by water. Even while consuming [poison], one who is protected by mantras and the like that remove poison remains unharmed.
18.81cd: Poison does not delude him; in the same way, the high-minded yogin [is not deluded]. 18.82ab: Thus has this been told, O Goddess; what else do you wish to ask?
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, on Supreme Vidyā, in the venerable *Mālinīvijayottara Tantra*.
Chapter Nineteen: The Authority on the Kula-cakra.

19.1ab: Then, having heard this supreme method of yoga, the daughter of Śaṅkara, with a serene countenance, bowed down to the Teacher of the World and spoke again. 19.1cd: [She spoke] after prostrating herself before the Guru of the Universe.

19.2ab: O Lord, Mālinī has been heard of as having distinct origins in her capacity as that which is to be accomplished (sādhya). 19.2cd: The three Vidyās, together with their ancillaries (vidyāṅgas), have been duly determined.
19.3ab: Now I wish to hear how she who is non-distinct (abhinnā) is accomplished.
19.3cd: For the benefit of the foremost of practitioners, you ought to speak out of your grace.
19.4ab: Thus addressed by Maheśānī, the Lord of the worlds, with respect, 19.4cd:
his lotus-face blossoming, replied with nectar-like words.

19.5ab: Desiring to propitiate Śambhu according to the procedure taught for his own lineage, the wise one— 19.5cd: The wise one should first worship the *kulacakra* by the path prescribed for initiation.
19.6ab: Thereafter, he should recite the supreme *śakti* mantra one hundred thousand times without interruption.
19.6cd: Situated within the enclosure of the seed-syllable of the other [deity], neither too fast nor too slow;
19.7ab: Likewise, one should recite her eight *khaṇḍas* a hundred thousand times each without interruption.
19.7cd: With undistracted mind, one should also recite the mantra of Kuleśvara six hundred thousand times.
19.8ab: Having performed the fire-oblation with a tenth part of the previously mentioned substance, the wise one, 19.8cd:
for one whose habit is constant mindfulness, the perfection of speech arises.
19.9ab: For one who is devoted to recitation within his own lineage, even if he is incapable of the ritual accomplishment.
19.9cd: O Goddess, in this cycle of existence, the attainments of enjoyments are inferior;
19.10ab: but one who is capable may accomplish middling or even supreme success.
19.10cd: Having performed the rite of service, he should wander the earth like a whirling leaf.
19.11ab: One should stay for five nights in a city, but for three nights in a town;
19.11cd: and having stayed for one night even in a village, one should perform this rite.
19.12ab: Whatever the first letter of a name, that belongs to the object within its respective class.

19.12cd: The families of cities and so forth have been described by those who know the ritual procedures; of this there is no doubt. 19.13ab: Whichever deity is established as the presiding one within a particular group, 19.13cd: that very deity should be meditated upon and worshipped as its lord by the practitioners.
19.14ab: Having respectfully approached some city or similar place belonging to him, 19.14cd:
and having stationed oneself in one's own directional sector, the wheel should be joined at its own rising; 19.15ab: [lacuna] ... when each has risen equally... [lacuna]
19.15cd: The deity is Māheśvara... [lacuna] 19.16ab:
Just as it is in sequence during the night... [lacuna] so it is by day. 19.16cd:
In his own direction and at his own rising, the wise man should meditate upon that very group.
19.17ab: He should remain until the rising of another [planet], and from there he should resort to his own direction.
19.17cd: Reflecting upon his own family, he should go to that very region or family. 19.18ab: As long as the practitioner remains in another direction, he should then contemplate that [other] one.
19.18cd: Thus, having wandered as far as its own station by the path described for the wheel of the family (kulacakra), 19.19ab: it returns again according to the sequence of the previous time.
19.19cd: Having arrived there, O Goddess, that mistress of the region and the family—
19.20ab: He should give some food and other such things, or have them given by someone else.
19.20cd: Engaged in this ritual method, with his conduct concealed and firm in his vows, 19.21ab: having attained the assembly of the Yoginīs, he attains perfection in just six months.
19.21cd: "O Goddess, this procedure is difficult to perform for those devoid of strength, the lowest of men.
19.22ab: It is the foremost bestower of all accomplishments throughout all the Kula scriptures.
19.22cd: Now, even in a single village, town, or city..."
19.23ab: Having taken refuge in that particular direction, one should mutter that very same *kula* [mantra].
19.23cd: Without effort, within three years, one shall accomplish the supreme fruit. 19.24ab: Having abandoned the ways of the world, accepting only a single morsel of food.

19.24cd: Or else, one should perform the mental rotation of the meditation-wheel (dhyānacakra), which is of the nature of the Kula, at the navel-center (nābhicakra). 19.25ab: One should effect this turning with the mind according to the sequence of all times. 19.25cd: Then, within half a year, the host of Yoginīs [will enter] the end of his body.
19.26ab: It manifests without doubt as the illuminator of one’s own consciousness.
19.26cd: By that mere manifestation, the yogi becomes a noble scion of the family of yogis.
19.27ab: O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, he even becomes the lord of yogis.
19.27cd: Or else, O Goddess, one should contemplate the eightfold sequence beginning with the letter *ya*.
19.28ab: [One should visualize it] in its own form, with a body formidable and agitated by rays of light.
19.28cd: In the center of that, one should recollect Kuleśāna, who awakens one's own consciousness.
19.29ab: Furthermore, the yogi, desiring the state of a Yoginī, should subsequently contemplate that entire [universe] as having become a wheel in the form of a lamp-flame. 19.30ab:
When this has become manifest, it is called "established in the body" (piṇḍastha) by the awakened one.
19.30cd: Then, O Goddess, the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) arises for him spontaneously. 19.31ab:
Likewise, [the states of] love, heroism, compassion, sorrow, anger, and so forth— 19.31cd:
this is declared to be "awakened" (prabuddha) and "situated in the mass" (piṇḍastha), O you who are worshipped by the immortals.
Then, for one who is engaged [in practice], after many days have passed,
the realization of the states of the principles (tattvas) beginning with Earth arises. They consider that supreme knowledge, known as *piṇḍastha*, to be "well-awakened."
19.33cd: Or else, one should visualize there a wheel with three times eight spokes (twenty-four spokes).
19.34ab: It is pervaded by the letters from *ka* to *ha*, its primordial form accompanied by the nasal bindu (*m*).
19.34cd: Performing everything there in the same manner as before, one shall obtain this fruit.
19.35ab: Or else, the yogin, while recollecting the sixteen-spoked [wheel] endowed with the first letter;
19.35cd: or by the middle sequence, the fifth [wheel] with the *cumbaka* and others;
19.36ab: there are seventy-two thousand channels (*nāḍī*) in the navel-wheel (*nābhicakraka*).
19.36cd: Because it attains the state of a *piṇḍa*, it is therefore called *piṇḍa*.
19.37ab: That which is to be known as abiding therein is declared to be *piṇḍastha*.
19.37cd: [Lacuna] ... [lacuna] ... [lacuna] ... hair ... [lacuna].
19.38ab: One attains freedom from fever within a year, even by chance.
19.38cd: For this "fivefold wheel" (cakrapañcaka) is situated in the heart, as previously described.
19.39ab: The wise proclaim that which is established in the "pada" to be the four Vedas.
19.39cd: O Goddess, that wherein there is the comprehension of meaning is called a *pada*.
19.40ab: Here, one should know the fourfold division consisting of fifteen types.
19.40cd: When the *sarvatobhadra* is successfully accomplished, it attains the state of being auspicious in every respect.
19.41ab: Freed from the defects of old age and death, he is a contemplator of yoga.
19.41cd: Even though pervasion is well-established, his range of perception extends below *māyā*.
19.42ab: He knows equality with its lord and attains mastery over it.
19.42cd: But when [the breath] is situated at the feet, one should not contemplate it as having the luster of the moon or the luster of a lamp.
19.43ab: One should contemplate that very [light] filling one's own body with a flood of nectar. 19.43cd: That this leads to the destruction of death—what is so wonderful about that?
19.44ab: This description of the lunar orb and so forth that has been uttered is merely illustrative;
19.44cd: in whatever form the Supreme Goddess is meditated upon, 19.45ab: through that very form, she bestows the desired fruit within the various divisions such as *piṇḍastha* and the rest.
19.45cd: Those who desire the auspicious form of Śiva, the remover of inauspiciousness, [seek it].
19.46ab: Because that which resides between the eyebrows is established therein, therefore— 19.46cd: The pentad, resembling the sun, is said to be situated in form.
19.47ab: There too, as before, accomplishment arises from the stages culminating in Īśvara. 19.47cd: But that which transcends form, O Goddess of Gods, has already been described in many ways.
19.48ab: Thus, this is the supreme pervasion of the Kula-cakra, stated in brief.
19.48cd: It has been taught for the sake of all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhi*) in the *Siddhayogīśvarīmata*.
19.49ab: Furthermore, it is always [taught] according to its divisions and through the distinctions of the individual phonemes (*varṇa*).
19.49cd: For the sake of the complete accomplishment of all things, beginning with the Vidyās, they desire the yoga of the yogins.
Furthermore, the distinction of the castes is proclaimed according to tradition:
having visualized in one's heart a female form adorned with white garments and the like,
seated upon the navel-cakra and possessing a radiance equal to ten million moons.

19.51cd: One should then contemplate incessantly that which is the seed of all scriptures; 19.52ab: emerging from one’s own mouth, one should reflect upon it as having the form of a shimmering string of pearls, filled with radiating rays of light.
19.53ab: With colors resembling stars, it begins with immeasurable radiance; 19.53cd: Within half a month, it unimpededly disgorges a collection of scriptures.
19.54ab: In a dream, one established in samādhi [attains this] after a month; after six months, according to one's desire.
19.54cd: Even scriptures that have been lost, whether in their textual form or their meaning, 19.55ab:
the yogin knows within a year, provided he has attained absorption in them (tanmayatā).
19.55cd: And this has been described in brief as an incidental fruit (anuṣaṅgaphala).

19.56ab: The attainment of equality with the Lords of Knowledge (vidyeśvara) and other supernatural powers (siddhis), 19.56cd: are now described according to their differentiation by each individual phoneme. 19.57ab: These should be constantly meditated upon by yogins who desire to enjoy those respective fruits.
19.57cd: By means of the application of the sequence of placement, according to all three paths;
19.58ab: whichever syllable, arising from the power of the *kula*, resides in a particular limb;
19.58cd: the knower of yoga, having established that very syllable right there in its own essential form, [should meditate].
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, the Section on the Wheel of the Kula (*kulacakra*), in the illustrious *Mālinīvijayottara*.
The twentieth chapter, the Determination of All Mantras, begins:
20.1ab: Now, the Śākta consciousness is described according to the divisions of the *piṇḍa* and so forth.
20.1cd: For the sake of the yogis' accomplishment of yoga, [this is taught] in brief and not in detail.
20.2ab: The "piṇḍa" is said to be the body; likewise, it refers to the nature of Śakti and Śiva.
20.2cd: It is celebrated as the bliss of Brahman, strength, splendor, heroism, and vitality.
20.3ab: That [Self], though beginningless, is obstructed by ignorance for the sake of the conscious self;
20.3cd: For its manifestation, everything that is unobstructed proceeds.
20.4ab: Being manifested by that [process], it abandons its prior state.
20.4cd: Those cognitions which one attains have been described above. 20.5ab: They desire that very state, because from it arises the comprehension of all objects.
20.5cd: Therefore, [that state] arises eternally and perpetually from the Śiva-self.
20.6ab: That very form is said to belong to the self, yet it is perishable.
20.6cd: They say that which transcends form is the supreme, being beyond the range of the senses.
20.7ab: Having paid homage to the teacher, the wise person should cultivate meditation upon that.
20.7cd: One should examine the object only so long as the state free from affliction has not been reached.
20.8ab: It is not thus, nor is it thus, nor even thus, nor yet even thus—clearly.
20.8cd: With a mind joined in yoga, one should continue until even this [conceptualization] is sufficient [to be transcended].
20.9ab: Having made oneself identical with that [reality], free from all sense objects and faculties, 20.9cd:
for as long as one remains even for a moment, trembling arises. 20.10ab: There is also dizziness, the onset of sleep, and a slight sense of bliss.
20.10cd: Therein, one should diligently fix the mind with the desire for the supreme fruit.
20.11ab: This very form of the Self has been made manifest by Śiva.
20.11cd: For therein, that which is to be known remains as being of the nature of Śiva.
20.12ab: One should understand that [the mantra] exists as a strengthener of that [divine form].
20.12cd: By constantly practicing that [mantra], through reliance on gross bodies and so forth, 20.13ab:
it attains a fourfold division, although it is inherently undivided by means of devotion.

20.13cd: The gross body (sthūlapiṇḍa) is said to be twofold, through the division of external and internal. 20.14ab: They maintain that the external is composed of the elements (bhautika), while the second is the subtle body (ativāhika).
20.14cd: By relying thereon first, the yogin, though possessing full consciousness, [perceives] clearly...
20.15ab: He fully grasps external objects and even some internal ones;
20.15cd: through the second support, he attains the reality of the nature of things.
20.16ab: And he clearly exercises mastery within his own body over the seats, fields, and so forth.
20.16cd: Whatever arises from the observation of its own true nature, 20.17ab: by steadying the mind upon that, one shall obtain all of it.
20.17cd: Therefore, out of a desire for the supreme, one should not perform this [other practice] there.

20.18ab: Released from the two bodies, yet still somewhat imbued with their latent impressions (vāsanā), 20.18cd: abiding within the state of pure consciousness alone (*vijñānakevala*), this is designated as the "stage" (*pada*).
20.19ab: For one who has reached this stage through the yoga of the sequence of consciousness,
20.19cd: One attains the state of consciousness that transcends the arising of forms.
20.20ab: This fourfold object of knowledge is to be understood through its fourfold reliance upon the objective referent.
20.20cd: And that [attainment] has as its limit the falling away from the prior realization of reality and so forth.
20.21ab: Free from the state of being a word, yet slightly following that [word], 20.21cd:
because it is the state of one's own essential nature (*svarūpa*) which brings about manifestation;
20.22ab: for that reason it is called "conformity" (*sārūpya*), since it is accompanied by that which is situated in form (*rūpastha*).
20.22cd: That [initiation] is also said to be fourfold, according to the divisions of "arisen" (udita) and so forth.
20.23ab: And by the arising of knowledge, O Goddess, it bestows its fruit through the sense of "mine-ness" (mamatva).
20.23cd: By means of this sequential yoga, one should join those [levels] within the intermediate states.
The mind attains the pure, supreme state that transcends form;
that [state] is said to be fourfold according to the distinctions in the fruits of realization.
Having practiced that threefold [path] with the desire for the fruit of all supernatural powers (siddhi),...
20.25cd: But having cast off the body from the fourth [state], one is liberated at that very moment.
20.26ab: Thus has the knowledge of Śiva been illustrated through the distinctions of the *piṇḍa* and so forth.
20.26cd: Now hear the collection of mantras and vidyās according to the rules for the practice of yoga.
20.27ab: Equipped with the previously mentioned ritual procedure, in the location previously enjoined, 20.27cd:
one should contemplate the supreme syllable (parārṇa) somewhere within the five locations beginning with the navel.
20.28ab: By its very nature, it illuminates the interior of the body with a mass of radiance.
20.28cd: With his intense radiance, [it extended] from there up to the world of Brahmā.
20.29ab: As he was thus recollecting, my dear, within seven days, 20.29cd: a truly great immersion into the power of Rudra (rudra-śakti) arose.
20.30ab: Possessed, he prattles many sentences in Sanskrit and other languages; 20.30cd: likewise, he performs loud laughter, singing, and even the wailing of Śiva.
20.31ab: With his mind possessed, he acts [thus], yet he does not know anything at all.
20.31cd: When he is thus liberated after one month, wherever he may look, 20.32ab:
there in every direction he beholds all the quarters filled with rays. 20.32cd: Whichever direction he gazes upon for six months, [he remains joined to it].
20.33ab: He perceives various forms within each [of those objects];
20.33cd: he should not fix his mind upon them, nor should he abandon his practice. 20.34ab: A yogin who acts in this manner becomes a coward or a madman.
20.34cd: Even though he has attained that state, the hero may again fall from power through negligence.
20.35ab: Within a year, he attains the perfection of yoga as desired by his mind. 20.35cd: He may then attain either the higher or the lower [state] beyond this, according to his wish.
20.36ab: One should meditate on the true nature of the assembly of Mothers, or the heart of Bhairava;
20.36cd: Or one should meditate on Navātman, or indeed on Ratiśekhara;
20.37ab: Or else the group of eight beginning with Aghorī, or those beginning with Māheśī.
20.37cd: Or else, by means of the divisions beginning with Amṛta, there are the Rudras or even the Śaktis.
20.38ab: All are declared to be equal in power, having arisen from the Śakti of Rudra. 20.38cd: Alternatively, the supreme division of those filled with nectar is now proclaimed.

20.39ab: One should fashion the mantra-vidyā as residing in the vital breath (prāṇa), pervaded by Parā, and individually illuminated; it is pervaded by the vital breath and serves as the seat of Parā. 20.40ab: One should contemplate the wheel of twelve spokes or the wheel of sixteen spokes.
20.40cd: Or else, O Goddess, it may have eight spokes, or three hundred;
20.41ab: Or it may have six spokes, O Mantra-knower—listen to how all this is so.
20.41cd: This has been explained in brief: together, there are two hundred and fifty wheels.
20.42ab: This [group] attains a state of threefold qualities through the distinction between the pairs of male and female deities.
20.42cd: Through the differentiation of rites such as pacification (*śānti*) and so forth, each [pair] possesses a twelvefold nature.
20.43ab: Dakṣa, Caṇḍa, Hara, Śauṇḍī, Pramatha, Bhīma, and Manmatha.
20.43cd: Śakuni, Sumati, Nanda, Gopāla, and then Pitāmaha;
20.44ab: Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Kālī, Karālī, and Vikṛtānanā; 20.44cd: Kroṣṭakī, Bhīmamudrā, Vāyuvegā, and Hayānanā.
20.45ab: Gambhīrā and Ghoṣaṇī—these twelve are proclaimed.
20.45cd: O Dear One, those beginning with Brahmāṇī are likewise situated in the four corners starting from the southeast (āgneyī).
20.46ab: Siddhi, Ṛddhi, Lakṣmī, Dīpti, Mālā, Śikhā, and Śivā.
20.46cd: Sumukhī, Vāmanī, Nandā, Harikeśī, Hayānanā, 20.47ab: Viśveśī, and Sumākhyā—these are the twelve [goddesses] in sequence. 20.47cd:
Their designators (vācaka) are to be known as the vowels, excluding the neuter ones.
20.48ab: And in the sixteen-spoked [wheel], there are Amṛta and the others, according to the distinction between the feminine and masculine readings.
20.48cd: Śrīkaṇṭha, Ananta, Sūkṣma, Trimūrti, and Śarvarīśvara; 20.49ab: Arghyeśa, Bhārabhūti, Sthiti, Sthāṇu, and likewise Hara.
20.49cd: Jhiṇṭhīśa, Bhautika, and likewise Sadyojāta; 20.50ab: Anugraheśvara, Krūra, and Mahāsena as the sixteenth; 20.50cd:
Siddhi, Ṛddhi, Dyuti, Lakṣmī, Medhā, Kānti, Svadhā, and Dhṛti.
20.51ab: Radiance, nourishment, intellect, fame, stability, good rebirth, and mindfulness;

20.51cd: and the sixteenth, Suprabhā—these are the powers (śaktis) beginning with Śrīkaṇṭha. 20.52ab: In the sixteen-spoked [cakra], the vowels are to be known as the expressive agents (vācakas) in every respect.
20.52cd: Likewise, in the eight-spoked [wheel], there are the deities beginning with Aghora and beginning with Aghorī;
20.53ab: And likewise, O Goddess, those beginning with Māheśī—listen now to these twenty-four;
20.53cd: All of them in sequence, beginning with Nandā, and likewise those beginning with Brahmāṇī.
20.54ab: Saṃvarta, Lakulīka, Bhṛgu, Śveta, and likewise Baka;
20.54cd: Khaḍgī, Pinākī, Bhujaga, and the ninth is Bali; 20.55ab: Mahākāla, Dviraṇḍa, Chagalāṇḍa, and likewise Śikhī.
20.55cd: Lohita, Meṣa, and Mīna, as well as those named Tridaṇḍin and Āṣāḍhin; 20.56ab: Umākānta, Ardhanārīśa, Dāruka, and likewise Lāṅgalin;
20.56cd: as well as Someśa and Śarman—these are considered to be twenty-four.
20.57ab: Those beginning with *ka* and ending with *bha* are to be known [as the letters] on the eight-spoked [wheel], while the group of eight beginning with *ya* [is on the six-spoked wheel].

20.57cd: The letter *ma*, existing in the form of a *bindu*, stands above all of them. 20.58ab: Furthermore, the syllable *juṃ* and likewise *svāhā* are placed in sequence as the six [syllables] on the six-spoked [wheel].
20.58cd: Bali, Balinanda, Daśagrīva, Hara, and Haya;
20.59ab: And Mādhava, O Great Goddess, is proclaimed as the sixth.
20.59cd: Viśvā, Viśveśvarī, Hārādrī, and Vīranāyikā.

20.60ab: The Yoginīs are remembered as six by means of those very seed-syllables (bījas), beginning with "Ambā" and "Gurvī. 20.60cd: All of them are mutually entwined according to the distinction between the Lord and his retinue (āvaraṇa). 20.61ab: From the letter *a* to the letter *kṣa*, they bestow the fruit of all accomplishments (siddhi).
20.61cd: For yogins and practitioners of mantras who are devoted to the practice of meditation, 20.62ab:
or else, in the midst of all the maṇḍalas (cakras), by reciting and meditating upon a vidyā as desired, 20.62cd: or a mantra previously specified, one attains success.
20.63ab: Thus has been taught in brief that which bestows the fruit of all desires.
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled "The Determination of All Mantras," in the illustrious *Mālinīvijayottara*.

The twenty-first chapter: On the Attraction of the Moon. Now, therefore, the supreme secret, the most excellent nectar of the knowledge of Śiva, is described for the destruction of disease and death for yogins.
21.2ab: In the sixteen-spoked wheel of the sky-farer (*khaga*), with its pericarp fashioned from the moon, 21.2cd:
one should meditate upon the Supreme Goddess (*parā*) there, flowing as nectar in her own essential form. 21.3ab:
Equipped with the previously mentioned ritual placement (*nyāsa*), the wise practitioner should remain thus for a single moment.
21.3cd: Then, having led the tongue upward, one should apply it to the uvula.
21.4ab: One should visualize the divine nectar flowing down, white as the orb of the moon.
21.4cd: His mouth becomes filled with a slight amount of saline water.
21.5ab: Because of its iron-like smell, one should not drink it there, but rather discard it;
21.5cd: One should practice this in this manner until it becomes palatable. 21.6ab: Then, by drinking that, one becomes free from old age and disease.
21.6cd: Within six months, without effort, one becomes a conqueror of death within a year.
21.7ab: Once a sweet taste has arisen therein, from that time forward, whatever substance one contemplates while staying there, 21.7cd: by that very thing one’s mouth is filled.
21.8ab: Blood, or wine, or else fat, or even milk;
21.8cd: Or ghee, oil, and so forth—any liquid substance—with undistracted mind.
21.9ab: Now I shall further proclaim another supreme procedure for the transference [of consciousness].

21.9cd: But when [the body] has died, one should enter the living body by means of the science of yoga. 21.10ab: Standing in a windless place, having mastered the vital breaths and the sequence of the rules for posture, 21.10cd: one should gradually effect the entry of the wind into a cotton wick from the sun.
21.11ab: One should perform the procedure for attraction through taste using jaggery and neem until [the desired result].
21.11cd: Then, having fashioned an auspicious image with sandalwood, jaggery, and camphor, 21.12ab: one should apply it to the limbs that are upright and free from defects.
21.12cd: Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) there as well, one should perform the piercing (*vedha*) very gradually.
21.13ab: One should effect the restraint (*nirodha*) there, and immediately after that, the friction (*ghaṭṭana*).
21.13cd: "Friction" (*ghaṭṭana*) is to be understood as the moving of the limbs and the minor parts of the body.
21.14ab: For that yogi thus practicing, who is disciplined in yoga, 21.14cd: that image wavers and even runs toward him. 21.15ab: He should impel it again until it has returned to its own place.
Standing on his side, he should move her again when she has fallen face up;
in this manner, with his whole being, he should continue until she has come under his control. From that point onward, the yogin may enter wherever he pleases.
Whether in a dead body or a living one, by means of the distinction between *saṃkrānti* and *ākrānti*,
the wise man should cast the net of power (*śaktijāla*) like water into all the joints of the limbs, and thus he should pervade every limb with power from each respective limb.

21.18cd: One should protect one’s own body, or else abandon it when under attack. 21.19ab: When one who has a firm aim may obtain even many bodies, 21.19cd: then, even while simultaneously relinquishing them, he takes them up without a doubt.
21.20ab: Now I shall further proclaim another [practice] that produces immediate conviction, 21.20cd: the divine nectar of meditative absorption (*samādhi*), which destroys death for yogins.
21.21ab: Named "The Attraction of the Moon," it bestows the enjoyment of the *vālya-yoga* within a month.
21.21cd: On the second day of the bright fortnight, when the sun is situated in Aries;
21.22ab: having bathed, being pure, fasting, and having performed the rites of worship, the wise one 21.22cd: should place the collection of lunar digits presided over by the Supreme.
21.23ab: Established in a place free from all disturbances, the wise one, 21.23cd: with a single-pointed mind and a tranquil self, meditating on the true nature of Śiva;
21.24ab: he should gaze at the moon until it has set.
21.24cd: Then one should eat with milk, while endowed with meditation upon the moon.
21.25ab: One should do this day after day until the fifteenth [lunar day] arrives.
21.25cd: For the remainder of the night, one should sleep while meditating on the Supreme Goddess residing within the lunar orb.
21.26ab: Likewise, on the full moon night, when midnight has arrived, 21.26cd: and when the people have fallen silent and all living beings are asleep, 21.27ab:
[he beholds her] resembling the rays of ten million moons and adorned with necklaces of bright pearls.
Clad in white garments, anointed with white sandalwood paste,
adorned with pearl ornaments, beautiful, and in the bloom of youth—
she is the goddess who bestows nourishment, streaming nectar from every side.
21.29ab: And one beholds the supreme Goddess seated upon a lotus throne, established in yogic sleep within the lunar orb; of this there is no doubt. 21.30ab:
Then, having pervaded her with the mind, the wise practitioner should draw her forth.
21.30cd: One should fix the mind firmly there as long as it has reached the tip of the mouth.
21.31ab: Then, opening the mouth, with a mind intent on meditation, 21.31cd: one should swallow it after drawing it in, and contemplate it once more within the heart.
21.32ab: By her having entered his body, the yogi becomes free from suffering;
21.32cd: having attained strength equal to hers, he may live as long as the moon and stars endure.
21.33ab: Even though being one, he may divide himself into many forms by his own will.
21.33cd: He enjoys the three worlds simultaneously, which have come under his control. 21.34ab: Having attained vast enjoyments, when the time of dissolution has arrived, 21.34cd:
he reaches the supreme nirvāṇa, which is difficult for those of unrefined self to attain.

21.35ab: Or else, if one is unable to contemplate that [form] in the sky, 21.35cd: one should meditate on it in a reflection, such as in water and so forth, as before. 21.36ab: Having drunk that with the mind, one should sleep through the remainder of the night while recollecting it.
21.36cd: "One attains, in six months, the unbroken state previously described.
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Attraction of the Moon," in the venerable *Mālinīvijayottara Tantra*.
The twenty-second chapter: On the Attraction of the Sun.
22.1ab: Now, O beloved, I shall tell you another supreme secret; 22.1cd: that unsurpassed nectar of yoga which has not been told to anyone.
22.2ab: Named "The Attraction of the Sun," it bestows the accomplishment of yoga upon practitioners.
22.2cd: It is perfectly accomplished within four months plus eight days.
22.3ab: One-eighth of a *prahara* is designated as a *nāḍikā*.
22.3cd: One should practice this daily, increasing the number of repetitions by one step each day.
22.4ab: This should continue from sunrise until sunset, as long as the sun is visible. 22.4cd: In a secluded place, free from all disturbances, one should perform the practice.
22.5ab: Having fasted for a day and night when the sun is situated in Capricorn, the yogi, having become pure, performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), and remedied the cold, 22.5cd–6ab:
Should place the wheel with eight, six, and twelve spokes upon the orb of the sun.
22.6cd: Endowed with the density of Śiva’s power and joined with the eight Bhairavas;
22.7ab: Joined with the years and so forth, the seasons, and the months, along with the lunar mansions and other [divisions];
22.7cd: One should contemplate the eight-spoked [wheel] within the image, and one should contemplate the remainder within the rays.

22.8ab: Having concentrated the mind there for the prescribed duration, the wise one, 22.8cd: with eyes not closed, should gaze at the orb of the sun. 22.9ab: Then, when that time has passed, with eyes well-closed,
22.9cd: One should enter a world within the midst of darkness that is free from disturbances.
22.10ab: There, with eyes opened wide, one perceives a form like a reflection.
22.10cd: Having fixed the consciousness there, one should remain until [the vision] ceases to be seen.
22.11ab: Even when the mind has perished, one should remain for the remainder of the time, recollecting [the practice].
22.11cd: Thus, O Goddess of the Gods, within a month that [vision] becomes stable.
22.12ab: Within two months, one perceives everything; there is no doubt in this matter.
22.12cd: With three [eyes], he beholds everything crowded with the solar orb.
22.13ab: At the conclusion of the time previously mentioned, while the hot-rayed sun is situated in Taurus, 22.13cd: he gazes upon the Supreme Lord within the solar orb, together with his discus.
22.14ab: Having drawn up what has been perceived, one should bring it to stability at the tip of the mouth.
22.14cd: Having swallowed it as before, one should afterwards bring the movement to a state of immobility.
22.15ab: There, having unified the self with that [element] for a moment, one should remain.
22.15cd: O Goddess of the gods, as long as he remains [there], for that long he abandons the earth.
22.16ab: While the multitude of people looks on, he goes together with the sun. 22.16cd: By this method, O Goddess, one becomes a lord of the masters of perfected yoga.
22.17ab: From Śiva down to the earth, it is nowhere obstructed. 22.17cd: Having enjoyed vast pleasures, one merges into the supreme, partless [reality].
22.18ab: This is that wheel of Khecarī, wherein one attains the state of moving through the sky.
22.18cd: This has been declared, along with its secret, in the *Siddhayogeśvarītantra*.

22.19ab: Alternatively, for one who first contemplates their own body in the form of a wheel, including both the exterior and the interior, 22.19cd: there will certainly be fruit for that person of resolute mind.
22.20ab: Or, while pronouncing the [syllables] beginning with *pha* and ending with *na*, which are radiant with sound, light, and wind;
22.20cd: the wise one, having rested the mind at the crown of the head for a single moment, 22.21ab:
by means of the application of the trident (*triśūla*), immediately abandons the earth.
22.21cd: Practicing in this manner, after one month he moves upon the earth like a wheel.
22.22ab: For a moment he touches the ground, and for a moment he is in the sky.
22.22cd: He utters the howls of a jackal and performs contortions and slapping sounds.

22.23ab: Or else, he may speak in many ways, such as by forming mudrās and so forth. 22.23cd: Having left the earth for six months, remaining in samādhi with firm senses, 22.24ab: the practitioner of yoga stands in the sky at a distance of one cubit.
22.24cd: He beholds the host of Yoginīs, characterized by manifold forms.
22.25ab: Having disciplined his self for one year, he becomes equal to them. 22.25cd: Even as the worlds look on, he illuminates the quarters with his splendors.
22.26ab: Having been drawn up from the surface of the earth, one becomes the lord of those who move through the sky.
22.26cd: This mudrā is called Khageśvarī in the Yoginīmata. 22.27ab: Or else, having remained awake for three days and nights without weariness, the yogi [attains this].
On the fourth day, at the beginning of the night, having worshipped Maheśvara,
the wise man, having performed the rite of protection in the thick darkness,
fixes his mind between the eyebrows for a moment and beholds.
22.29ab: Resembling light in form, he sits upon a seat in the lotus posture;
22.29cd: One who is disciplined in yoga should constantly practice this very application.
22.30ab: Within a single month, one perceives whatever object exists inside a house.
22.30cd: By means of two [months], everything situated outside [the city] is perceived; by three, that situated within the city;
22.31ab: by four, that situated within the district; and by five, up to the limits of the mandala.
22.31cd: By six months, the great yogi perceives the fissures of the earth.
22.32ab: One attains omniscience within a year; there is no doubt about this.
22.32cd: Established in the pervasive presence of the true being of the assembly of Yoginīs and Siddhas, 22.33ab:
the one whose self is united with yoga perceives [it] and becomes equal to them.
22.33cd: By this very procedure, seated in the svastika posture, 22.34ab:
having abandoned the various kinds of *bindu*, one should contemplate the pure form. 22.34cd:
Through that as well, one attains all the aforementioned supreme fruit.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, the Section on the Attraction of the Sun, in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara Tantra;
[now begins] the twenty-third chapter.

23.1ab: Now, therefore, I shall tell you now this supreme secret, 23.1cd: which produces immediate realization for the sake of yogic accomplishment for yogins. 23.2ab: Equipped with the previously mentioned placement (*nyāsa*), one should fix the mind upon the ear.
23.2cd: In a place free from wind or with very little wind, and devoid of external sounds;
23.3ab: then, in that state, this yogi hears an unobstructed sound, 23.3cd: like that of a very pure bell-metal vessel being struck here again and again.

23.4ab: Having heard which, O Great Goddess, one is liberated from both merit and sin; 23.4cd: having concentrated his consciousness there, the best of those who know yoga, within six months, 23.5ab: understands even the cry of a flock of birds clearly and without effort.
23.5cd: From afar, the cognition of hearing arises for him within one year;
23.6ab: And within three years, the attainment of the fruits of all desires occurs. 23.6cd: That he succeeds—what wonder is there? He succeeds without effort.
Alternatively, during the month of *grahaṇa*, having placed the sun behind him,
equipped with the previously described placement (*nyāsa*), and leaning slightly against a wall,
he should observe his own shadow above the head at the *anāhata* [cakra].
23.8cd: With his inner self absorbed in that [image] as it emerges from the incense stick, 23.9ab:
the one engaged in yoga attains identification with it to whatever degree; 23.9cd: to that same degree, a great proficiency arises within him.
23.10ab: Then, there [he sees] a great radiance resembling shimmering rays;
23.10cd: upon seeing which, even once, the destruction of all sins occurs.
23.11ab: Through practice of that, within a month, it spreads everywhere.
23.11cd: He perceives all directions as having a form filled with garlands of flames.
23.12ab: By practicing for six months, the yogi shall attain omniscience.
23.12cd: Having become a divine body after one year, he rejoices for a long time like Śiva.
23.13ab: Now the seed-syllables (jāti) shall be proclaimed, together with their former seats and eternal [forms]:
23.13cd: Hrīṃ, Kṣlāṃ, Kṣvīṃ, Vaṃ, and likewise Āḷkṣaṃ—these are for the first pentad in due order.
23.14ab: Haṃ, Yaṃ, Raṃ, Laṃ, and likewise Vaṃ—for the second pentad.
23.14cd: *ṛṃ*, *ṝṃ*, *ḷṃ*, *ḹṃ*, as well as *oṃ*, *auṃ*, *haḥ*, and *aṃ* [are placed] up to the edge of the pericarp (*karṇikā*).
23.15ab: On the filaments (*kesara*) are the letters ending in *bha*: *haṃ*, *hāṃ*, *hiṃ*, *hīṃ*, and likewise *huṃ*.
23.15cd: *hūṃ*, *heṃ*, and *haiṃ* are on the petals; thus are the powers (*śakti*) by their own respective names.
23.16ab: In the three mandalas, one should fashion the remaining subtle form of the preta. 23.16cd: The syllable *jra* is proclaimed for the prongs of the trident. 23.17ab:
In all cases where a specific seat has not been mentioned in the application [of the ritual], one should employ this very one.

23.17cd: *Namaḥ*, *svāhā*, likewise *vauṣaṭ*, *huṃ*, *vaṣaṭ*, and *phaṭ* are the [six] classes [of mantras]. 23.18ab: In all rites of expiation (*prāyaścitta*), one should recite the rosary without interruption.
Whether it be broken or unbroken, having considered the relative strength and weakness [of the mantra],
one should begin with a single recitation and continue up to three hundred thousand, O Dear One;
beyond that, there is nothing superior anywhere, provided it is performed with the restraint of the vital breath.

23.20ab: For those who are always inclined toward wandering to external *pīṭhas*, *kṣetras*, and so forth, 23.20cd: I shall now fully explain the practice that bestows the fruit of easy accomplishment.
23.21ab: The Great Breath (*mahāprāṇa*), conjoined with the nose (*nāsā*) and marked with a bindu, takes the form of a staff (*daṇḍa*).
23.21cd: In the same way, one should keep this secret; this knowledge is considered to consist of two syllables.

23.22ab: Having performed service to it according to the previously mentioned rule, with a tranquil mind, 23.22cd: one should wander through the sacred seats (*pīṭha*) and so forth for the sake of accomplishment, and not otherwise, O Goddess worshipped by heroes.
23.23ab: Having reached that place, one should respectfully encircle oneself with mantras;
23.23cd: one should surround the site with the Vidyā using a red thread.
23.24ab: With a single-minded focus in many ways, the wise one [should do so] both externally and internally.
23.24cd: Then, in a certain field there, yoginīs of terrifying prowess, 23.25ab: having assembled, bestow their respective oral transmissions (*saṃpradāya*).
23.25cd: By means of which oral transmission, O lady of virtuous vows, as soon as it is obtained—
23.26ab: Having become equal in power to that [deity], one enjoys desired enjoyments.
23.26cd: Or else, having performed service, the wise one should recite [the mantra] one hundred thousand times.
23.27ab: Having offered libations with a tenth part [of that number], he should employ it for minor rites.
23.27cd: Merely by being uttered there, this [mantra] becomes a destroyer of poison.
23.28ab: Revolving like a wheel, one should visualize this [mantra] as red within the womb. 23.28cd: Or else, by the sequence of going and coming, it is restrained by the [lacuna] drop.
23.29ab: Remaining there, by quickly contracting the mass [of the body] through withdrawal, 23.29cd: one who is single-minded may in an instant agitate even Urvaśī.
23.30ab: Or else, having performed the rite of service, by means of three hundred thousand recitations, |||
23.30cd: Satisfied by the lotus, the glory-fruit, she bestows great fortune.

23.31ab: Seated upon a throne arisen from the six [syllables], even when accomplished according to the stated path, 23.31cd: the goddess becomes the granter of all success for the practitioners of mantra.
23.32ab: Having set aside the ritual for the trident-lotus and the seven [mantras] beginning with Navātman, 23.32cd:
the wise one should provide the sixfold arising seat (āsana) in every ritual of the wheels (cakras).
23.33ab: And the "small" and "great" [mantras] should be joined with the heart-seed (hṛdbīja) for the ritual service (upacāra).

23.33cd: Now I shall further explain another unsurpassed knowledge of dreams. 23.34ab: Having become absorbed in that within the heart-cakra at night after night with undistracted mind, 23.34cd: after one month, O Great Goddess, whatever one perceives in a dream—

23.35ab: That becomes true for that yogin who is engaged in meditation; 23.35cd: provided that he remains devoted there according to the regulation of time. 23.36ab: Then, during the first watch of the night, within a year, [he perceives] the auspicious and the inauspicious.
23.36cd: Gradually, within six months, [one attains the results] in sequence on the second and subsequent days.
23.37ab: At the time of dawn, one shall obtain the fruit within ten days.
23.37cd: This applies likewise whether the rite is preceded by a formal resolve (saṃkalpa) for others or for oneself.
23.38ab: When a certain task has arisen, one should employ the knowledge of the sleeping state.
23.38cd: Thus, O Goddess, this Siddhayogīśvarīmata has been told.
23.39ab: There is no knowledge higher than this within the sphere of existence from Śiva down to the earth.
23.39cd: He who knows this according to reality is Śiva; there is no doubt about this.
23.40ab: The dust of his feet, when placed upon the head, serves for the pacification of sin.
23.40cd: Having heard this, the Great Goddess attained supreme satisfaction.
23.41ab: Thus he asked for forgiveness, prostrating himself again and again.
23.41cd: In this way, I have related to you all of the *Mālinīvijayottara*.
23.42ab: This unsurpassed nectar of yoga was told to me by the Goddess.
23.42cd: This great [teaching] must not be told by you even to those who are not your disciples.
23.43ab: Nor should it be given to the disciples of others without having first examined them with diligence.
23.43cd: This has been fully declared for those whose souls delight in the practice of yoga.
23.44ab: For those who have set forth, who are disciplined, and whose minds are dedicated solely to Śiva;
23.44cd: having obtained from Kārttikeya this great nectar of knowledge;
23.45ab: the sages, practicing yoga, have attained supreme perfection.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter in the venerable *Mālinīvijayottara Tantra*;
and this great tantra named *Mālinīvijayottara* is completed.
